newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply down, no support in sight.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply down, no support in sight.

text.p: FCOJ futures continued to lose ground Friday on mixed selling and a dearth of buying interest, which pressured prices to fresh contract lows across the board, floor sources said.
The trade and the speculators were cited as the day's major sellers, while the speculators were also noted as light scale-down buyers.
Prices slid nearly the five-cent daily limit in several contracts, ending down 4.00 to 81.85 in most-active March, having ranged from 87.00 to a new low of 81.85 cents.
January fell 4.30 to 78.10, after sliding to a contract low of 78.00. The back months closed down 4.00 to up 1.05.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 7,500 lots.
A record Floirda crop projected in 1996/97 and warm weather forecast throughout the citrus belt, weighed heavily on today's market.
Buzz Lopez, an assistant meteorologist with Smith Barney, said temperatures will remain in the 50s and 60s (degrees Fahrenheit) for the next six to 10 days.
"There is no indication of any cool air going into Florida," Lopez said. "There may be a cool-down next week, but temperatures will remain in the upper 40s."
Meantime, the U.S. Department of Agriculture put the crop at 220 million 90-lb boxes, in its latest estimate.
On the charts, firm technical support does not exist despite an oversold market, analysts said, pegging the next downside target at 83.80 cents in March.
Paine Webber analyst Bernard Savaiko said the market could find short-term support near the bottom of a channel around 82.00 cents in March.
"I'm not saying a bottom would be in place but theoretically, the market could find some temporary support," he said.
Savaiko cited 65.45 cents, a ten-year low on the monthly charts made in Feb 1993, as a downside target.
